judge: Two judges, each a Claude agent shown only the match sheet's claims and truth, not which method made the claims, ruled on every claim without seeing each other's rulings. An adjudicating agent ruled on each claim where they differed. Rules: the same problem at the same place; a general claim states nothing; when unsure, no match.

matches.note: The claim is about allowable height, area and fire ratings missing from the code summary. No truth item covers this.

Adjudicated: Same defect: the claim says the building has one stair where two are required, which is the 'too few stairs' defect. Same place: the claim covers 'the building and each story' and calls the building 5-story, so it covers floors 4 and 5. Rule 2 only rules out a match at a different floor, and floors 4 and 5 are inside the claim's scope. The G1.1 sheet field shows where the tool put the claim, but the statement itself covers every story. This is not a rule-3 general claim, because it states a definite stair count without hedging. The claim also says floors 1-3 fall short, which the truth does not record. That makes the claim partly wrong but does not change that it states the floor 4 and floor 5 items.
The claim is about the EXIT 1 door swing and its missing tag. No truth item covers this.
The claim is about the exit enclosure being combined with HALL 225. No truth item covers this.
The claim is about the elevator opening into the exit enclosure. No truth item covers this.
The claim is about door ratings in the schedule. No truth item covers this.
The claim says travel distance and dead-end lengths are not dimensioned. It does not say a named floor has too few stairs.
The claim says no site plan is provided. This is no site plan.
The claim is about accessibility information that is not shown. No truth item covers this.
The claim is about emergency escape openings. No truth item covers this.
The claim says EXIT 1 has no matching door tag. No truth item covers this.
